checks.description: An absolute http(s) link resolves (after its redirect chain) to 2xx or 3xx. 404, 410, 403, timeout, and network failures are flagged; a 403 counts as broken (never distinguished from a real dead link).
A link's redirect chain contains a permanent redirect (301 or 308). Counted as drift. A temporary redirect (302 or 307) is recorded as informational only and never counted.
Every npm/pypi package named in an install command exists in its registry.

A version pinned in an install command lags the registry's real latest (same-major = stale-pin, major-behind = version-drift), or the registry's latest is itself marked deprecated (npm) or yanked (PyPI).

Fenced code blocks (json, bash/sh/zsh/shell via `bash -n`, js/ts via the TypeScript compiler when installed, python via python3 ast.parse) parse. Blocks with an ellipsis marker are skipped as intentional fragments; console/text fences are ignored; a missing optional parser (e.g. no `typescript` peer) never produces a finding.
An environment variable or command-line tool used inside a code block is never mentioned in prose anywhere on the page. Copied verbatim from onboarding-transfer-rate's L1-prereq-order rule.
A relative path (in prose or code) that resolves within the repo tree points at a file that does not exist there. Own repos only — no repo tree exists for site or external pages.
A documented `npm run <script>` names a script absent from the target repo's package.json. Own repos only.
The README's stated Node.js version requirement does not match the repo's package.json engines.node. Own repos only.
Prose contains an unresolved placeholder marker. Flag only — never a proposal.

redirected-link.safe_to_auto_apply_when: every hop status is in {301,308}, the final status is 200, the host is unchanged or only a scheme or leading www. differs, the final path is not '/' unless the original path was also '/', and the final URL matches none of /login|signin|404|not-found/i
redirected-link.proposed_unsafe_when: the final host differs from the original host (cross-host permanent redirect)
redirected-link.flag_only_when: the original URL's path is '/' (a root redirect is reported, never auto-rewritten)

stale-pin.safe_to_auto_apply_when: the registry's latest version shares the same major as the pin
stale-pin.flag_only_when: the registry's latest version is itself marked deprecated (npm) or yanked (PyPI)

version-drift.proposed_unsafe_when: the registry's latest major differs from the pinned major
version-drift.flag_only_when: the registry's latest version is itself marked deprecated (npm) or yanked (PyPI)

broken-relative-path.safe_to_auto_apply_when: exactly one file in the repo tree shares the broken path's basename
broken-relative-path.proposed_unsafe_when: never (path-rewrite is safe or flag, no unsafe-but-proposed middle state)
broken-relative-path.flag_only_when: zero or more than one file in the repo tree shares the basename (candidates are listed in evidence)

missing-prerequisite.proposed_unsafe_when: always, when the gateway returns content
missing-prerequisite.flag_only_when: the gateway call errors (llm.errors counted; no proposal emitted)

broken-link.flag_only_when: always (a dead link is never guessed at)

http-get-final.description: A fresh GET against the proposal's `verify:` URL returns 200 with 0 redirect hops.

registry-version-exists.description: A fresh npm/pypi registry lookup returns 200 for the proposed version and it is not marked deprecated/yanked.

tree-path-exists.description: The rewritten relative path resolves to a file that exists in the committed repo tree listing.

recheck-patched-text.description: The originating check no longer fires against the patched page text, and no new counted finding appears.

patch-applies.description: applyUnifiedDiff(raw) === expected for every proposal's diff; for repo-file targets, `git apply --check` also succeeds against a snapshot copy of the target file in $TMPDIR.

pass_definition: A proposal passes re-verification when patch-applies succeeds AND its category's specific reverify method succeeds (or the category has no specific method, in which case patch-applies alone decides).
headline_template: Across {pages} documentation pages ({own} of Ryan's own: {repos} public repos and {site_pages} getsmartai.ai page(s); {ext} external quickstarts snapshotted 2026-09-11) with {links} links, {snippets} code blocks and {pins} version pins, {drift} drift findings; {proposed} fixes proposed, {verified} ({p}%, 95% Wilson CI {lo}-{hi}%) pass independent re-verification.
sub_headline_template: Of the {proposed} fixes proposed, {safeAuto} are safe to auto-apply without human review; {simulatedCount} finding(s) rely on an LLM judgment ({simulatedTag}, confidence capped at {cap}) and are never auto-applied.

stats.rule: pct is wilson(verified, proposed); a proportion is never printed without its interval; proposed=0 means pct is null and the headline generator refuses

not_measured: snippet execution (parsing only; nothing is run)
prose quality of any generated fix
semantic correctness of any fix (only mechanical re-verification, never meaning)
a 403 is counted as broken, never distinguished from a genuinely dead link
